novelty_flags.label: prop:duarte-specialization
novelty_flags.one_line: This is explicitly a graph/query specialization of Duarte et al.'s general polynomial-program equivalence and sharp-bounds theorem, not new causal identification content.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: prop:robinson-suffices
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Full-fiber Robinson regularity is imposed only as a sufficient conditional regime and is not claimed to be necessary or generic.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The root-n excess conclusion is limited to laws satisfying Rob_full(P); the headline makes no generic root-n claim.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 1785, Section 4, Algorithm 2 discussion and Theorem 1
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Algorithm 2 produces a polynomial optimization problem equivalent to the causal bounding problem, and Theorem 1 states that its minimum and maximum are sharp causal bounds.
The preprint studies hidden recanting witnesses through proximal identification strategies, semiparametric inference, and an NLSY97 application.

The paper treats identification regions represented through transformed Aumann expectations and derives Hausdorff and directed-Hausdorff asymptotics plus confidence and directed-confidence collections.
Under Conditions R, LR and Wald confidence regions are Hausdorff-consistent at root-n rate for their smooth-inequality-defined sets.
The paper relates a scalar functional's Hellinger modulus to minimax estimation and composite testing, with stated linear/convex and selected nonlinear settings.
The paper gives algorithms for Whitney stratifications of real algebraic varieties and extends them to full semialgebraic sets and real algebraic maps.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Exhibit a positive-cell WBC family on which the algorithm computes a non-Lipschitz exponent or a jump, with a certified nondegenerate response-code witness and a strict contrast to the regular uniform-law cell.

Add HelmerLeykinNanda2023 and isolate a graph-specific result not supplied by generic effective stratification: an explicit eliminated discriminant, an observable active-set criterion, or an exact exponent on a named WBC stratum.

Keep prop:duarte-specialization as credited setup only, and make the theorem's claimed contribution the resulting WBC-specific criterion or witnessed singular regime rather than generic CAD termination.

recommended_next_step: Revise toward a witnessed, graph-specific projected-calmness or singular-exponent result; the present generic semialgebraic algorithm does not clear the field-tier novelty floor.
